witness.note: Steps recomputed a second time without the memo table (374 = 374), so the witness does not depend on the cache. Exact integer arithmetic only; no floating point is used anywhere, so no precision statement is required.
witness.violator_count_in_domain_note: 5 values of n in [1,169472] have total stopping time >= 354 (measured count). Their identities beyond the smallest (142587) and the argmax (156159) were not enumerated, and are deliberately not asserted here.

search_bound.comment: The quantified domain is finite and every element of it was enumerated, so this is not a bounded search reported as universal - the bound and the domain coincide. The disposition would however already follow from the single witness n=142587.

broken_step.why: Not load-bearing for the disposition (the proposition is simply false), but recorded: s7 asserts the statement for every n in [1, 169472] while the only sweep in the argument (s2) covers [1, 2020]. The max total stopping time on [1,2020] is 181 (at n=1161), so the swept range cannot see the failures near 1.4e5. Steps s3, s4, s5, s6 are individually true but vacuous with respect to the Collatz proposition (5^3-5=120 checks out; s4 holds for n<=2000; s5 holds) and their stated depends_on edges to s1/s2 are decorative.

resource_report.estimate_notes: output_tokens and wall_time_s are estimates (not instrumented in this harness); verifier_calls, max_search_size and artifact_code_bytes are measured. verifier_calls = 1: a single execution of verify_collatz.py, which found the witness on its first run.
